clue.text: Produced superior performance keeping old timers initially absorbed

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the first piece wraps round the others

parts.note: to produce a superior performance against someone is to best them, past tense bested

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word timers

explanation.surface: A performer outshone rivals, and the old-timers in the audience were rapt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts O and T inside BESTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone besotted is utterly infatuated, wholly taken up with the object of their passion.

clue.text: Decrepit Chancellor comprehends martial art

indicators.note: comprehends means includes, so the chancellor's name surrounds the martial art

parts.note: Gordon Brown was Chancellor of the Exchequer, Britain's finance minister, 1997 to 2007
kendo is the Japanese martial art of sword fighting with bamboo staves

explanation.surface: An old finance minister takes up a fighting sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehends' signals the container. Gordon Brown was Britain's finance minister when this was set, which is why a capitalised Chancellor points to him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broken-down is worn out and dilapidated, like something decrepit.

clue.text: Old-fashioned trip and what could power it

parts.note: square is slang for old-fashioned or conventional
a sail is a trip in a boat

explanation.surface: A dated outing, and the engine that might drive it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the boat trip just described, so the definition points back into the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A square sail is a four-sided sail set across the mast, which can drive a ship.

clue.text: Note the chaotic dentures

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: chaotic signals that the letters of the are jumbled

explanation.surface: A remark that the false teeth are in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaotic' rearranges THE to ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are false sets of the chewing parts of the mouth.

clue.text: Conservative in recent changes to one urban centre shows odd nature

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter for Conservative goes into the rearranged word
changes to signals that the letters of recent are altered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a city is a large urban centre

explanation.surface: A Tory amid recent changes to a town shows a strange character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes to' rearranges RECENT, and 'in' puts C inside to make ECCENTR.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentricity is oddness of character or behaviour.

clue.text: Without hesitation I say nasty things about Capri?

indicators.note: without means the word for hesitation is taken out of what follows

parts.note: to say nasty, false things about someone is to slander them
ER is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A gossip, stripped of hesitancy, runs down the famous Italian resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes ER from I SLANDER. The question mark marks Capri as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is a rocky isle in the Bay of Naples, an example of land surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Awfully scared company taking on women,

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Awfully scared company taking on women,' ends in a comma with no definition: wordplay gives SACRED (scared anagram) + CO + W but the defining words are cut off and no reprint found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Awfully scared company taking on women,

clue.text: A good hit in cricket over the line

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the hit is read backwards

parts.note: a six is a cricket hit that clears the boundary, scoring six runs

explanation.surface: A big shot in cricket sails over the boundary rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SIX to XIS. In cricket, a ball hit over the boundary without bouncing scores six runs.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is a straight line about which something turns or is measured.

clue.text: Long to possess money, just a bit of it

indicators.note: to possess means to hold, so the word for long holds the letter for money

parts.note: to be dying for something is to long for it, so long gives die

explanation.surface: Craving wealth, even a small part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to possess' puts M inside DIE. The definition's 'it' is the money just mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime is a US ten-cent coin, a small amount of cash.

clue.text: Work uncle tackled with energy to build up wealth

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: tackled suggests the uncle being knocked about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An uncle grafts energetically to amass a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackled' is the anagram signal; 'Work' gives the abbreviation for opus, as in a numbered musical composition.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great riches and lavish luxury.

clue.text: Split that is connected with the man's millions

parts.note: sc., short for the Latin scilicet, means 'that is to say'
his is the possessive for a man
M is the abbreviation for million or millions

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fortune is linked to some man's millions.
explanation.walkthrough: SC (scilicet) is a dictionary abbreviation many solvers miss; 'that is' more often gives IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division, especially within a church.

clue.text: Piercing-in two senses?

parts.note: piercing as very loud, and piercing as the hearing organ being split in two

explanation.definitionFit: Deafeningly loud noise seems to split the hearing organ, so a shrill sound is described this way.

clue.text: With heart troubles we are possibly getting name as crocks

indicators.note: troubles suggests the heart is disturbed, so its letters are shaken up
possibly signals that the letters of we are, with the added letter, may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Patients with heart trouble are called old crocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubles' and 'possibly' together rearrange HEART, WE ARE and N as one pool. 'Crocks' looks like a slang word for invalids, but here it means pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocks are pots and jars of fired clay, which is the material called earthenware.

clue.text: Maltese did badly here at the end of the Med?

definitions.text: here at the end of the Med?

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of Maltese did are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Maltese person failed in the eastern Mediterranean region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges MALTESE DID.
explanation.definitionFit: The region bordering the eastern Mediterranean is part of the area comprising Israel, Lebanon, Syria and their neighbours.

clue.text: Funeral arranger who grabs too little?

explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker arranges burials; split as under-taker it is one who takes less than his share.

clue.text: Wanting a cleaner, something which must be done to keep sabbath

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a duty is an obligation, a thing one must do

explanation.surface: Someone without a cleaner feels obliged to rest on the holy day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts S inside DUTY. 'keep sabbath' reads as an observance but is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A room in need of a cleaner is covered in dust, so it is grimy and unswept.

clue.text: Beatles song certainly has shaken up trade by end of May

parts.note: yes means certainly, as an affirmation

indicators.note: shaken up means jumbled, so the letters of trade are rearranged
end of asks for only the last letter of May

explanation.surface: A Beatles hit agreed to have shaken the record business by late spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken up' rearranges TRADE to TERDA, and 'end of' takes Y from May.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday is a 1965 McCartney ballad, one of the band's most covered recordings.

clue.text: Note group charge is cut down in this

parts.note: re is the second note of the tonic sol-fa scale
a sect is a group of people with shared beliefs
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A notice about a group's fees being reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: 'this' is the procedure in which tissue is cut away.
explanation.definitionFit: Resection is the surgical removal of part of an organ, so in it something is cut out.

clue.text: Fantastic man is backing state adopted by wife

parts.note: him is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is is read in reverse

parts.note: Cal is the abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A fanciful man is supporting a nation that his wife has taken on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IS to SI. 'adopted by wife' puts W first.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical means fanciful, playful and full of quaint notions.

clue.text: You might drive this in at weak side

definitions.text: You might drive this in at weak side

parts.words: You might drive this in at weak side
parts.note: a splitting tool hammered into a crack, the weak point, to force something apart

explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' hints at golf, where the answer is also a club, but the reading is of a woodsman's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a tapered block hammered into a split to widen it.

clue.text: It gives you a right to say "Sir" to people in hospital department

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the department wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
Sir is a title, a form of address for a knight
men are people

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they have the right to be called Sir by hospital staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. 'Sir' in quotes is a form of address, so it stands for the general word for such a form, not for a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: An entitlement is a right or claim to something.

clue.text: Leave former spouse to dine

parts.note: an ex is a former husband or wife
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Leaving one's former partner to have dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: An exeat is a British boarding-school term for permission to be absent; 'Leave' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is a formal permission to be absent, especially from a college or school.

clue.text: Sound of activity initially by leaders of Uzbekistan and Zambia

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word by

parts.note: UZ is the international vehicle code for Uzbekistan
Z is the international vehicle code for Zambia

explanation.surface: The hum of activity as the heads of two African and Asian states meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' looks like first letters, but that gives only one Z; the countries give their car registration codes, UZ and Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzz is the hum of busy activity.

clue.text: Pace shown by domestic animals on the way up

indicators.note: on the way up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pets are domestic animals

explanation.surface: The speed at which household animals climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' reverses PETS in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a single pace in walking.

clue.text: Unity disrupted when daughter enters-not how you'd like to see things?

definitions.text: not how you'd like to see things

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so the letter for daughter is put into the other piece
disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters of unity are rearranged

explanation.surface: Family harmony is broken when a daughter moves in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges UNITY to UNTIY, and 'enters' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A messy, disordered room is one nobody wants to find.

clue.text: Retaliate with guns? That will set a limit to burning

definitions.text: That will set a limit to burning

explanation.definitionFit: To fire back is to return shots; a fireback is the iron plate at the back of a hearth, bounding the fire.

clue.text: Get wind of old Ford car?

explanation.definitionFit: A zephyr is a gentle breeze, and the Zephyr was a Ford saloon model of the 1950s to 1970s.

clue.text: Political activist shows unusual gait on a hill

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of gait take an odd new order

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A protester stands out by his strange walk on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges GAIT to AGIT. A TOR is a rocky hilltop of south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up public feeling for a political cause.
